For example, suppose that $a =_r b : A$ and $b =_s c : A$. Their composite
$a =_{r;s} c : A$ records the route through $b$. Reversal gives
$c =_{s^{-1};r^{-1}} a : A$, and the empty trace $1_a$ witnesses reflexivity.
The traces $r;r^{-1}$ and $1_a$ have the same endpoints; identifying their
witnesses requires a structural cancellation rule. A different witness
$a =_u c : A$ is not determined by $r;s$ merely because both establish the
same endpoint equality. A declared rewrite between these parallel witnesses
is additional information. The endpoint judgement establishes that $a$ equals $c$; a rewrite between
$r;s$ and $u$ establishes equality of their witnesses.

Earlier work studies the resulting weak groupoid, whose structural laws hold
through rewrites of computational paths
\cite{DeVerasRamosDeQueirozDeOliveira2025weak}. The topological application of
labelled natural deduction uses these operations to calculate fundamental
groups of the circle, torus and real projective plane
\cite{DeVerasRamosDeQueirozDeOliveira2025topological}. The book
\emph{Computational Paths: The Calculus of Equality}, by Ramos, de Queiroz,
de Oliveira and Gabbay, gives a broader account of the explicit-witness
programme \cite{RamosDeQueirozDeOliveiraGabbay2026}. We use that programme as
background for a geometric fragment with presentation-controlled rewriting.
Our hypotheses concern continuity and geometric soundness of the declared
rules; they impose no general normalization or decision procedure on an
arbitrary presentation.

It is also useful to package the derived integer normal forms as a completed
presentation with a primitive step $\lambda_n$ for each $n\in\Z$,
\[
  \lambda_n(t)=[tn].
\]
Its named rules are the derived integer rules
\[
  (n;m)\RwEq(n+m),\qquad 1_0\RwEq 0,
  \qquad (n)^{-1}\RwEq(-n).
\]
This integer-indexed presentation packages normal forms already derived
from the single generator.  The proof of the finite-generator classification
does not use it.
